subtype: Approach: groupthink on the first idea [Pitfall]
passage: At the first meeting, Vinay said, "Fake-review detection. Public dataset from an online shop. Done." He said it so quickly and firmly that everyone nodded, including Ira, though she had never seen such a dataset. Manoj wondered too. Both kept silent, each assuming the others had checked. For three weeks they wrote code against a sample file Vinay had emailed. Then in the canteen Manoj put down his tray. "Ira, can I ask something stupid? Where is the full dataset?" Ira laughed with relief. "I've been looking for two weeks. It doesn't exist." They walked to Vinay's table. He went quiet. Three weeks of work sat on a single small sample, and the deadline was not moving.

qa.q: What topic did Vinay suggest at the first meeting?
qa.a: Vinay suggested fake-review detection using a public dataset from an online shop.

qa.q: What is Ira feeling when Manoj asks about the full dataset?
qa.a: Ira feels relieved, laughing because she has doubted the dataset for weeks and now hears someone else say it.

qa.q: What alternative approach could the team have used at the first meeting, and why?
qa.a: They could have asked everyone to name one worry before deciding, because private doubts come out early when each person is invited to speak.

qa.q: How might Vinay have felt when Ira and Manoj arrive at the table?
qa.a: Vinay probably feels embarrassed and surprised, going quiet when the doubt appears after weeks of work.

grounding: Shows groupthink: the first idea is accepted without questions while two members privately doubt it, and the doubt surfaces only after weeks.

passage:
"So, status update. Aditya, you had the dataset?"
"Working on it."
"It's week seven."
"Look, Suraj, a dataset of street-food hygiene photos from Indian cities is out there somewhere. I've emailed three labs."
"Any replies?"
"...Not yet."
Hafsa put her pen down. "Can I say something? I wasn't sure this dataset existed even in week one."
"Then why didn't you say?"
"Because you were so sure, Aditya, and everyone clapped. It felt rude."
Suraj rubbed his face. "I had the same doubt. I searched for two nights in week two and found nothing. I thought I was just bad at searching."
"So two of you knew?"
"Suspected. We should have said it out loud."
"Okay. Seven weeks gone. What now?"
"Now we talk to the guide tomorrow, and look for a topic with data we can actually see."

qa.q: What week is it at the status update?
Why did Hafsa stay quiet at the start?
qa.a: Hafsa felt it would be rude to question Aditya, who seemed so sure and everyone clapped, so the doubt was swallowed.

qa.q: What else could the team have done in week one?
qa.a: They could have asked each member to write doubts privately before agreeing, and checked that a dataset existed before committing.

qa.q: How might Aditya feel hearing that two teammates doubted it all along?
qa.a: Aditya may feel embarrassed and a bit hurt that nobody spoke up earlier, when changing course would have been easy.

grounding: Shows a team going along with the loudest member's topic while two members privately doubt the dataset exists, a doubt that surfaces only after weeks.

subtype: Approach: groupthink on the first idea [Pitfall]
passage: In our final year, Karan suggested a project predicting bus arrival times in our city from live GPS data. He was so excited that we all said yes in the first meeting. I'm Seema. That night I tried to find the live bus data. I couldn't. I told myself it probably needed special access and Karan must know how. My friend Sarika, it turned out, had the same doubt; she had searched for an hour and found only old timetables. Neither of us said anything. It felt disloyal to question the idea everyone loved. For six weeks we built screens and wrote the literature review. Then our guide asked, "Where is your data from?" Karan went pale. There was no live feed we could use. We had to change the topic in week seven and redo half the work. Looking back, two quiet doubts in week one could have saved six weeks.

qa.q: Why did Seema keep quiet about the doubt?
qa.a: Seema felt it would be disloyal to question the idea everyone loved, and hoped Karan must know how to get the data.

qa.q: What else could the team have done in the first meeting?
qa.a: They could have made checking the data source the first task before saying yes, and invited everyone to voice doubts openly.

qa.q: How might Karan have felt when the guide asked about data?
qa.a: Karan went pale, likely shocked and embarrassed that his exciting idea had no usable data behind it.

grounding: Illustrates a team accepting the most enthusiastic member's topic while two members quietly doubt the data exists, until the problem surfaces weeks later.
